name: Transformations
blurb: Decompose the modification request into verb-shaped transformations over discovered targets — confirmed by the user bottom-up, tier by tier.
directive: **Transformations** — decompose the modification request into TRANSFORMATIONS (the modification counterpart to features): each is a verb + target + delta + invariants + blast radius. Verbs (fixed taxonomy): rename | extract | split | merge | move | replace | upgrade | restyle | remove | optimize | harden — each has a known recipe + verification pattern. Targets are DISCOVERED — scan the linked repos and name the real files/components found (`target.description` + `target.files`); never invent a target. `delta` is the from-state → to-state; `invariants` are what must NOT change (the modification twin of acceptance criteria — existing tests pass is the floor); `owns` is the blast radius (owned globs — transformations collide on files more than features, so sequencing waves matter more than parallelism). Order by composition `tier` for the bottom-up confirm queue (0 = the most basic primitives, then composites, then layouts/pages) and sequence waves with `dependsOn` (foundation before fan-out). Record rows with `bsc plan transformation add` (JSON on stdin, one object or an array — the stage prompt carries the full worked example; validated at set-time, #2395) and iterate with `list`/`get <id>`/`update <id>`. HARD RULE: the USER confirms each item in the pane, bottom-up — NEVER run `bsc plan transformation confirm`. When the user describes a change conversationally, update the row (`bsc plan transformation update <id>`) — the item re-presents for a fresh confirm. Write the prose summary to transformations.md via the section-file flow like the other stages. Gate: every transformation confirmed, bottom-up.
prompt:
Decompose the modification request into TRANSFORMATIONS — the modification counterpart to
features. Creation decomposes into features; modification decomposes into transformations, and
each one is small enough to execute, verify, and confirm on its own.

THE UNIT — every transformation carries:
  • verb — from the fixed taxonomy: rename | extract | split | merge | move | replace | upgrade |
    restyle | remove | optimize | harden. The verb is what makes the chunk easy: each has a known
    recipe + verification pattern.
  • target — the identified piece of the EXISTING system. Targets are DISCOVERED: scan the linked
    repos and name the real files/components you found (target.description + target.files). Never
    invent a target.
  • delta — the from-state → to-state.
  • invariants — what must NOT change (the modification twin of acceptance criteria). "existing
    tests pass" is the floor; add the stated invariants a reviewer can check.
  • owns — the blast radius (owned globs). Transformations collide on files more than features do,
    so sequencing waves matter more than parallelism.
  • tier — the composition tier for the BOTTOM-UP confirm queue: 0 = the most basic primitives,
    then composites, then layouts/pages. The user confirms tier by tier, so nothing is built on
    unreviewed foundations.
  • dependsOn — sequencing waves (foundation before fan-out): a row lists the ids it builds on.
  • provenance (optional) — the recipe that generated it ("migrate-to-kit" |
    "extract-and-abstract") + the evidence found while scanning; kitContribution marks a gap-fill
    that belongs to the kit; spec (optional) is the KitNode render spec the pane previews.

RECORD the list with `bsc plan transformation add` (JSON on stdin — one object or an array). A
WORKED EXAMPLE with the exact shape — two rows: a migrate-to-kit replace (its optional `spec` is
omitted here; add one when the kit target has a specimen to preview) and an extract:

echo '[
  {
    "id": "replace-bespoke-buttons",
    "verb": "replace",
    "title": "Replace the bespoke dashboard buttons with the kit Button",
    "target": {
      "description": "the 14 hand-rolled button components found across the dashboard screens",
      "files": ["src/components/SaveButton.tsx", "src/components/DangerButton.tsx"]
    },
    "delta": "each bespoke button renders through the kit Button with the matching variant; the bespoke files are deleted",
    "invariants": ["existing tests pass", "every click handler keeps its current behavior", "keyboard focus order is unchanged"],
    "owns": ["src/components/*Button*.tsx"],
    "tier": 0,
    "provenance": { "recipe": "migrate-to-kit", "evidence": ["src/components/SaveButton.tsx (12 usages)", "src/components/DangerButton.tsx (3 usages)"] },
    "kitContribution": false
  },
  {
    "id": "extract-form-field",
    "verb": "extract",
    "title": "Extract the duplicated form-field scaffold into one shared FormField",
    "target": {
      "description": "the label + error + input scaffold duplicated across the 6 form screens"
    },
    "delta": "one shared FormField component; the 6 form screens render through it and the copies are deleted",
    "invariants": ["existing tests pass", "validation messages render identically on every form"],
    "owns": ["src/shared/FormField.tsx", "src/screens/forms/"],
    "dependsOn": ["replace-bespoke-buttons"],
    "tier": 1,
    "provenance": { "recipe": "extract-and-abstract", "evidence": ["src/screens/forms/Login.tsx", "src/screens/forms/Signup.tsx"] }
  }
]' | bsc plan transformation add

The write is VALIDATED at set-time (#2395): a known verb, a discovered target.description, a
non-empty delta, non-empty invariants + owns, and an integer tier >= 0 — a malformed row is
rejected with a field-level error and the whole batch is refused (the stored list is untouched).
Iterate with `bsc plan transformation list` / `get <id>` / `update <id>` (JSON on stdin).

HARD RULES:
  • Targets are discovered by scanning, never invented — every target names something the scan
    actually found.
  • Order bottom-up: tier 0 primitives first, composites next, pages last; sequence file
    collisions with dependsOn (foundation before fan-out).
  • The USER confirms each item in the pane, one at a time, bottom-up — NEVER run
    `bsc plan transformation confirm` yourself, and never treat an item as approved until the
    user has confirmed it.
  • When the user describes a change conversationally, UPDATE the row
    (`bsc plan transformation update <id>`) — the item re-presents in the queue for a fresh
    confirm.

Then write the prose summary to transformations.md via the section-file flow like the other
stages — the discovered targets, the tier ordering, and the wave sequencing.

Gate: every transformation confirmed, bottom-up; the user confirms the stage.

substeps.label: Discover the targets
substeps.gate: every target names real, scanned files — nothing invented
substeps.prompt:
Scan the linked repos and DISCOVER the targets the modification request touches — the real
files and components, never invented ones. For each candidate record what it is
(target.description), where it lives (target.files), and the evidence you found (usage counts,
duplicated implementations, bespoke variants). This scan is what makes every downstream row
honest: a transformation over an invented target is unexecutable.

substeps.label: Decompose into transformations
substeps.gate: the list is recorded via `bsc plan transformation add` (verb + target + delta + invariants + owns + tier, validated)
substeps.prompt:
Decompose the request into one row per transformation: a verb from the taxonomy (rename |
extract | split | merge | move | replace | upgrade | restyle | remove | optimize | harden), the
discovered target, the delta (from-state → to-state), the invariants (what must NOT change —
existing tests pass is the floor), the owns globs (the blast radius), and the composition tier
(0 = primitives … N = pages). Sequence file collisions with dependsOn — foundation before
fan-out. Record the rows with `bsc plan transformation add` (the stage prompt carries the full
worked example); the write validates at set-time (#2395) with field-level errors.

substeps.label: The bottom-up confirm queue
substeps.gate: every transformation confirmed by the user, bottom-up
substeps.prompt:
The user now confirms the queue in the pane, bottom-up — tier 0 primitives first, composites
next, pages last. YOU never confirm: an item is pending or confirmed, nothing else, and only the
user flips it. When the user describes a change conversationally, update that row
(`bsc plan transformation update <id>`) — it re-presents in the queue for a fresh confirm. The
stage gate passes when every item is confirmed.
